name: Undercut & Rally (U&R)

card.context: A leader, RS 80 or more, above its 200-day and above a 50-day that is not falling. Best right after a correction as the market turns up, especially when the index itself undercuts and reclaims a big support. Green or Yellow.
card.pattern: A level everyone can see (a bounced swing low, the 10-session range low, a rising 20 EMA or 50-day, a prior high or round number) is undercut by at most 6% after a close above it, then taken back within 3 sessions.
card.trigger: PREV LOW RECLAIM: a market order as price trades back above the level, confirmed intraday by an opening-range break, a VWAP reclaim, a 30-minute pivot or red to green; or near the close of a reclaim day that closes in its top half.
card.stop: A few cents under the undercut low, the lowest low while price was under the level. More than 3% away: size down or skip. The intraday entry near the level is what keeps it small.
card.failure_mode: The reclaim does not hold: a close back under the level, then the undercut low breaks, usually as the index breaks down. Most hits are stopped; the edge is the R of the few that run.

criteria.statement: Price $10 or more and at least $20 million traded a day (the dossier uses a 20-day average; the glossary's shared window is 50).
criteria.evidence: TE ($3) and OPEN (about $6.50), two owner-praised U&Rs, fail it and stay out of the lessons. The public scanner has no floor; the internal one uses $2 and $10,000.

criteria.statement: The position is under 1% of average daily volume.
The buy-day close is above the 200-day SMA.

options.basis: B26 as it stands: no buy under the 200-day (the dossier's rule line)
allow a reclaim that closes back above the 200-day the same day
a washout U&R under the 200-day as a parabolic long (a burst down) under B26's exception

criteria.evidence: Morales's best U&Rs come at market turns, often near the 200-day, and Bracco's leaders reclaimed near their 200-day moving averages. The test: below the 200-day did about as well as above it (26% to 3R either way). A recent IPO has no 200-day at all (FIGR). The register's default: B26 as written, the washout cases stay as reading drills.

criteria.statement: The 50-day SMA today is at or above its value 10 sessions ago, and the buy-day close is above the 50-day SMA (a MAU&R of the 50-day reclaims it by definition).
criteria.evidence: The owner's RBRK pass (I did not like the declining moving averages) and his note that an undercut below the MAs is just not something I generally do. The 10-session test and the 50-day as the line are the dossier's proposal; the 50-day is also the internal scanner's gate.

criteria.statement: RS rating 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups.

options.basis: a leader setup, RS 80 or more always (the dossier's rule line; the owner's RS names and liquid leaders)
two kinds: the leader U&R (RS 80 or more, house trims) and the washout U&R (no RS rule, quick exit): Bracco's mean reversion play

criteria.evidence: The owner trades U&Rs on RS names and liquid leaders. Bracco calls his washout U&Rs a mean reversion play, which C31 exempts. The register's default puts the washout U&R in the exempt class with an RS line that held up as the cue. The test had no RS series; the 50-day and 200-day tests stood in.

criteria.statement: No earnings report in the next 3 sessions and no pending buyout or deal.

measure.and: no pending buyout or deal news

criteria.evidence: The owner on U (2026-11-08): held off due to earnings; my hard rule, as soon as there is buyout stuff I take it off my list. An earnings-reaction U&R (ZS) is after the report, so it is allowed.

criteria.statement: A Green or Yellow market reading; Orange only for A+; Red: mostly cash, plus shorts below the 200-day.

measure.what: the app's market reading on the trigger day

criteria.statement: Best right after a correction, as the market turns up, and especially when the index itself undercuts and reclaims a big support.
criteria.evidence: Morales: in conjunction with a market turn to the upside after a period of correcting. Bracco: the RS names that briefly undercut those previous lows and reclaimed in April 2025. Measured: slightly better with SPY under its 50-day (+0.10R against +0.04R), within about one standard error. Failures LULU 2020-02-24 and NVDA 2024-04-05 were correct-looking U&Rs as the index broke down.

criteria.statement: The level L is one of: a swing low (under the 3 lows before it, not above the 3 after it) that price then bounced at least 5% off, 5 to 60 sessions before the undercut; the lowest low of at least the prior 10 sessions; a rising 20-day EMA or 50-day SMA the stock closed above the session before; a prior high, a breakout level, the gap-up day's low, or a round number at one of these.

value: a 3-bar swing low bounced 5% or more, 5 to 60 sessions old
the lowest low of the prior 10 sessions or more
a rising 20-day EMA or 50-day SMA closed above the session before
a prior high, breakout level, gap-up day's low or round number at one of these

options.basis: only prior lows and base lows (Morales, S1, S2)
those plus rising moving averages, the MAU&R (S2); the register's default, plus gap lows
any obvious level, including prior highs, round numbers, gap lows and VWAP (the owner's PLTR $170, IREN $50, NBIS $141, MXL); the dossier's rule line

criteria.evidence: Measured (the internal one-day rule, E2): the 10-session range low was the only variant that beat its baseline (+0.13R against +0.03R); a held 21 EMA +0.06R, a held 50-day +0.05R. The swing-low numbers (3 bars, 5%, 5 to 60 sessions) are the dossier's proposal from Morales's prior low in the pattern and EdgeRater's 5% category. The owner's words: $160 flat, quick shakeout below the base.

criteria.statement: The prior day's low alone is not a level. A dip under only yesterday's low is an Oops, not a U&R.

measure.what: the level L is only the prior session's low

criteria.dossier_ref: 8.1 item 5, not enough on its own; 10 question 2
criteria.evidence: Measured: the prior-day-low variant of the internal rule (78,055 events, most of its fires) was flat against its baseline (+0.00R). The owner on a tiny undercut: a little subtle and hidden. The register's default: the prior day's low alone does not count; the Oops already owns it.

criteria.statement: A fresh, visible undercut: the session before the undercut closed above L; the low then trades under L.

measure.what: close of the session before the undercut

criteria.evidence: Wyckoff, Morales and Turtle Soup all describe a break that fools the crowd; a level already lost days ago traps nobody. The scan required it.

criteria.statement: Shallow: the undercut low is no more than 3% under L for an A grade and no more than 6% at all. Deeper is not this setup.

measure.note: 3% or less for an A grade

options.basis: no number, judgment only (Morales refuses one)
3% for an A grade, 6% at most, back above within 3 sessions (the dossier)
an ATR limit, for example 1 ATR (the register's default for an A: within about 1 ATR, back above the same day; up to 6% and 3 sessions as a B)

criteria.evidence: Measured (E1): undercuts 6% or deeper had the worst results (-0.09R, 16% to 3R) and 10.6% stops; 3% to 6% +0.01R; 0% to 1% +0.08R with 1.6% stops. Scan (rescanned 2026-11-10 with fills at the reclaim; the earlier figures used the open): an undercut of 3% or less reached 3R 51.1% of the time and 5R 40.5%, against 37.8% and 22.3% for one deeper than 3% (up to 6%); was 35.5% against 36.9% to 3R and 24.9% against 21.4% to 5R, so the earlier 'no difference' is gone. Median undercut in the scan 0.67%.

criteria.statement: Brief: price closes back above L the same session or within the next 3; no more than 3 closes under L. Longer is a Remount.

measure.what: closes under L from the undercut to the reclaim

criteria.evidence: Wyckoff quickly reverses; Turtle Soup same day, Plus One the next day; Deepvue's bars same day; the journal template a day or two. The 3 is the dossier's. Scan (rescanned 2026-11-10 with fills at the reclaim; the earlier figures used the open): a same-day reclaim reached 3R 53.8% of the time against 43.2% for one that took 1 to 3 sessions (was 31.3% against 43.2%); the same-day median stop is 0.58% against 1.87%, so most of the gap is the tight stop; measured: one session later did no worse, so same day is a preference, not an edge. 71% of first undercuts of a bounced swing low closed back above within 3 sessions. The glossary closes the gap: the U&R family runs to 4 closes, the Remount starts at 5.

criteria.statement: Volume is not required. Light volume on the undercut (under the 50-day average) is a grade-up.

options.basis: required on the reclaim: the journal template's rising volume
not required: Morales (Volume is generally not a factor), Wyckoff's quiet spring as a grade-up, and the test

criteria.evidence: Measured: reclaim-day RVOL 1.5 or more did slightly worse (+0.01R against +0.07R under 1.0); a reclaim on more volume than the undercut was only a hair better (+0.11R against +0.06R). Three of the ten examples broke on 0.61x to 0.73x volume.

criteria.statement: Option A, the owner's way: a market order as price trades back above L during the session, confirmed by an intraday turn: an opening-range-high break, a VWAP reclaim, a 30-minute pivot, or red to green.

measure.and: an intraday turn: opening-range break, VWAP reclaim, 30-minute pivot, or red to green

options.basis: the intraday reclaim with an opening-range, VWAP or 30-minute confirmation (the owner's practice: ARM very tight risk, TEAM clean 30 min pivot, QQQ opening ranges)
the close of a strong reclaim day
both, with (a) as the default (the dossier's recommendation)

criteria.evidence: Measured, Table C (a buy a cent over the level, an upper bound): every R number rose (+0.30R against +0.07R at the close; stop within 3% +0.60R). None of the 13 owner-named examples had a stop within 3% when bought at the close; FIGR was 1.6% from Bracco's fill. Scan (rescanned 2026-11-10 with fills at the reclaim; the earlier figures used the open): the fill at L plus a cent gave 50.2% to 3R and 39.2% to 5R on 66,020 hits (was 35.6% and 24.7%); with a stop of 0.5% or more, 47.1% and 33.8%.

criteria.statement: Option B, for someone who cannot watch: buy near the close of a reclaim day that closes in the top half of its range (DCR 0.5 or more).

measure.what: (close - low) / (high - low) of the reclaim day

criteria.evidence: Measured: top-half closes followed through 68% of the time against 43% for bottom-half closes. Scan (rescanned 2026-11-10 with fills at the reclaim; the earlier figures used the open): a reclaim day closing in its top half reached 3R 54.7% against 39.5% (was 42.4% against 17.7%). The knowledge-base template's strong close on reclaim day.

criteria.statement: Option C, IBD style: buy only when price clears a set distance over the old low (the shakeout-plus-three). A later, higher entry with a wider stop; not the default.
criteria.evidence: IBD's buy is three points over the old low. The dossier does not recommend it as the default.

criteria.statement: Never buy the undercut itself before the level is back.
criteria.evidence: Morales (rallies back above it), Turtle Soup (a buy-stop slightly above the previous 20-day low), IBD's shakeout-plus-three, the journal template (Enter on the reclaim, never on the undercut). One school differs: Wyckoff's tutorial allows a partial long on a low-volume spring itself.

criteria.statement: At the buy, price is no more than 4% over L.
criteria.evidence: The buy point is the level. After a big reclaim day the close can be well over 4% from L (DELL 2026-08-07, HOOD 2025-04-07). WYNN 2013-11-21 gapped back above L and filled at the open 0.4% over it; STLD 2022-02-24 opened 0.4% over L, dipped under and came back the same day, so its fill is L plus a cent, not the open (rescanned 2026-11-10).

criteria.statement: At the buy, price is no more than 10% over its 10-day average.

options.basis: C29 wins (the rule as written)
exempt U&Rs of an earnings-day low in the first week after the gap
measure the stretch from the level instead of the 10-day average for this setup

criteria.evidence: Rarely binds: 20 of 25,310 E1 events. The conflict is the post-earnings U&R: the owner's MXL (day three undercut of earnings day low at $50) was 40.9% over its 10-day. The dossier states no lean; the register's default measures a catalyst-day entry against the 10-day as of the prior close for days 1 and 2 and applies C29 from day 3.

criteria.statement: Write L, the stop and the size before the open.
criteria.evidence: The owner's plans name the level ahead (QBTS $15, RDDT $141.30, HPE $59); the buy waits for the reclaim.

criteria.statement: A few cents under the undercut low, the lowest low while price was under L.

measure.value: a few cents under the lowest low while price was under L

criteria.evidence: Turtle Soup: just below today's low; the owner: Stop at LOD, a stop at the new established support. Not the public scanner's 1.5% under the low, not the internal scanner's exact low, and not VoSI's 1 to 2% below the line for the MAU&R: the undercut low is the price that proves the trap wrong.

criteria.statement: If that stop is more than about 3% from the entry, size down (A5 does it) or skip. Never move the stop up to make it fit.
criteria.evidence: On a close entry the median stop was 2.6% (E1) and 1.7% (E2), but none of the 13 owner-named examples was within 3% from the close; they fit A13 only with the intraday entry near the level. Scan (rescanned 2026-11-10 with fills at the reclaim; the earlier figures used the open): a stop within 3% beat a wider one (51.5% against 37.3% to 3R; was 37.6% against 27.1%); median stop 0.88% (was 1.73%). LULU 2020-02-24: a 2.70% stop from a buy at L plus a cent (3.97% from the open in the earlier scan, over the line).

criteria.statement: A real stop order with the broker. It only moves up.
A gap through the stop: the first 30-minute low is the new stop; out if past 2R.

measure.what: loss at the first 30-minute low of the gap-down day

criteria.statement: Stop to breakeven once the trade has made 2R to 5R, at the first trim by default.

measure.what: R at which the stop moves to the entry

criteria.statement: A third off at 3R.
criteria.evidence: Eight of the ten examples reached 3R within 2 days; WYNN took 8. The journal template's first piece into the prior high is not the house rule.

criteria.statement: A third at 5R.
At the open if it gaps past a trim level.
Trail the last third: a close under the 10-day average for fast movers, the 21-day for steadier ones.
criteria.evidence: The owner's older habit (June 2025): trail the rest with a stop below the 9 and 20 period moving averages. The rulebook of 2026-11-09 governs.

criteria.statement: Under 1R after 10 sessions: out.
criteria.evidence: In the replay the median house result was -1R in every group but one: most trades are stopped, and the mean comes from about one trade in ten that makes 3R or more.

criteria.statement: The washout (mean-reversion) U&R: Bracco holds these 1 to 3 days and covers some on the bounce. A separate plan for it needs a ruling; the house defaults apply until then.

measure.what: holding period of Bracco's washout U&R

options.basis: house defaults (3R and 5R, trail the 10 or 21-day) for all U&Rs (the dossier's rule line; the register's default for every swing setup)
a quicker exit for the mean-reversion kind (Bracco: short lived trades and not meant to be held longer than 1-3 days)

criteria.evidence: Bracco on UAMY: these are short lived trades and not meant to be held longer than 1-3 days; FIGR: covered some on the bounce.

criteria.statement: No close back above L within 3 sessions: a breakdown, not a U&R. No trade.

measure.what: sessions from the undercut without a close back above L

criteria.evidence: The number is the dossier's; the vision rubric's disqualifier: a sustained breakdown, not a shakeout. Five or more closes under the line is a Remount.

criteria.statement: After the buy, a trade under the undercut low is the exit.
criteria.evidence: NVDA 2024-04-05: a 2.05% stop, reached 0.67R and was stopped two sessions later at 83.02 as the April 2024 correction began; a top-half-close reclaim like this one fails to reach 3R about 45% of the time (54.7% reach it, rescanned 2026-11-10).

criteria.statement: A close back under L after the buy is the early warning (the trap failed). Hold to the stop and do not add.
criteria.evidence: The journal template: It reclaims the level, then closes back below it. The trap failed, and the sellers were right. The dossier's options were sell at that close or hold to the stop; it recommended hold (A4), and the register's D-136 settles 29:8 the same way.

criteria.statement: A new try only on a new trigger, at most 3 a week and 6 a month on one stock.
criteria.evidence: The owner retries (ARM, NBIS) and knows the limit: NBIS just got shaken out too many times in the one $150 to $140 zone. AMD 2021-09-14: the stop did its job; a new try needs a new trigger, not a hold through the loss.

a_plus: ur.leader: a leader, RS 90 or more, in a top group
ur.trend_not_falling: above a rising 50-day and 200-day, averages stacked
ur.level: the low of a multi-week base, a prior breakout level or prior high, or a rising 20/50-day that has held before
ur.depth: visible but shallow, 3% or less, back above within 1 to 2 sessions (ur.reclaim_window)
ur.trigger_close: the reclaim day closes in the top half or better, clearly back over L
ur.volume_not_required: light volume on the undercut
ur.market_turn: turning up after a correction, or the index doing its own U&R; Green (ur.market_reading); in Orange only if everything else grades A+ (F65)
ur.stop_width: 3% or less from the entry
b_minus: ur.leader: RS 80 borderline, a middling group
ur.trend_not_falling: the 50-day falling or price under its averages (normally a pass: RBRK)
ur.not_prior_day_low: only the prior day's low, or a level price has crossed many times (a chop line)
ur.depth: 3% to 6% deep, or a full 3 sessions under (ur.reclaim_window)
ur.trigger_close: the reclaim day closes in its bottom half (follow-through 43%)
ur.volume_not_required: heavy selling that keeps coming
ur.market_reading: Yellow (smaller and fewer), or the index breaking down
ur.earnings_window: a report within a week
no_trade: ur.market_reading: Red (mostly cash, plus shorts below the 200-day); Orange below A+
ur.inv_no_reclaim: no close back above L within 3 sessions
ur.never_buy_undercut: the undercut itself, before the level is back
ur.not_stretched: more than 10% over the 10-day average
ur.earnings_window: a report within 3 sessions, or buyout news
ur.liquidity: under $10 or under $20 million a day
ur.retry: a fourth try in a week on the same stock

lookalikes.tell: Name the level. If it is one swing low at least 5 sessions old that price rallied 1 ATR off, on its first break, it is the 2B; if it is a rising 20 EMA or 50-day, a prior high, a round number or the 10-session range low, it is a U&R.

Look at the open and the level. An Oops opens under the prior close, trades under yesterday's low and reclaims the prior close the same day; a U&R needs a level that matters more than yesterday's low, and the reclaim may take up to 3 sessions.

Look left for a flat range. A spring undercuts the floor of a sideways range of 15 sessions or more that was touched at least twice, and closes back inside the same day or the next; a U&R's level can be one low, an average or a prior high, and it may take 3 sessions to close back above.
Count the closes under the level. Up to 3 closes under and then back above is a U&R; 5 or more closes under the line is a Remount, bought on the retake with the stop under the remount day's low.

For a moving average: a U&R of the 20 EMA or 50-day closed above the line the session before the undercut and is back above it within 3 sessions; a Remount of the 50 or 200-day has lost the line for at least 5 closes, one of them 0.5 ATR or more under it.
Name the level. If it is the gap-up day's low of a still-open 4% gap on 2x volume, it is Gap Support, the same mechanics at that one line with its own card; any other level is a U&R.

Measure the undercut and the averages. A U&R goes at most 6% under its level in a stock above its 50-day and 200-day; a capitulation is a 2 ATR flush on 2x volume under the 5, 9 and 20-day with the burst boxes checked.

invalidations: Before the trigger: no close back above L within 3 sessions, a breakdown (ur.inv_no_reclaim).
Before the trigger: the undercut is deeper than 6% (ur.depth).
Before the trigger: the 50-day is falling or price is under its averages (ur.trend_not_falling); under the 200-day (ur.above_200).
Before the trigger: earnings within 3 sessions or buyout news (ur.earnings_window).
Before the trigger: more than 4% over L or 10% over the 10-day (ur.no_chase, ur.not_stretched).
After the buy: a trade under the undercut low is the exit (ur.after_entry_stop).
After the buy: a close back under L is the warning; hold to the stop, do not add (ur.close_back_under).
A new try only on a new trigger, at most 3 a week and 6 a month (ur.retry).
mistakes: Buying the undercut before the reclaim.
Calling every dip under yesterday's low a U&R (that variant was flat; the owner: a little subtle and hidden).
Buying the close of a huge reclaim day and thinking the risk is tight (DELL: 8.3% from the close).
Chasing more than 4% over the level.
Ignoring an earnings date or buyout news (U).
Endless retries in one zone (NBIS: shaken out too many times).
Waiting for a volume surge that the setup does not need.
Mixing it up with its cousins: the Remount (a long stay under a line), Gap Support (the gap-up low), the Oops (a gap open under the prior low), the Go Signal (hourly), the 2B (any failed extreme).

short_mirror.note: The failed breakout, or upthrust (dossier 8.6): price trades above an obvious high (a prior swing high, a base high, a falling 20-day or 50-day) and closes back under it. Short as it trades back under the level; stop a few cents over the high of the poke; only below the 200-day SMA (B26), in a weak stock (RS 20 or less, C31) that is easy to borrow (D48). Wyckoff: a UT is the opposite of a spring; Turtle Soup: SELLs are reversed. Morales covers his shorts at undercuts of prior lows, so a short sitting in a stock undercutting an obvious low is exactly who this setup traps. Whether to teach it here or leave it to the Wyckoff (35) and 2B (28) lessons is D-001 (29:14).

best_conditions: A Green or Yellow market reading (F65). Best of all right after a correction, as the market turns up, and especially when the index itself undercuts and reclaims a big support (Morales's market turn; Bracco's April 2025 leaders). Measured: slightly better with SPY under its 50-day, not by much more than the noise.

management.trail: a close under the 10-day for a fast mover, the 21-day for a steadier one (E52)
management.breakeven: between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default (B19)
management.gap_open: a trim level the day opens past is taken at the open (F63)
management.gap_against: the first 30-minute low is the new stop; out if past 2R (B20)
management.overrides: none by default. Pending D-013: whether the washout (mean-reversion) U&R gets Bracco's 1 to 3 day hold with a trim on the bounce. Not ours: the scanners' 2R and 3R targets, the journal template's first piece into the prior high and raise the stop to the reclaimed level after a day.

base_rate.window: 60 sessions forward, fixed stop 5 cents under the undercut low, no trims, no breakeven, no trail; 1984 to 2026; the level is the lowest low of the prior 10 sessions; the fill at L plus a cent on the reclaim day (also when the day opened over L before the undercut), or the open on a gap back above after a day under; one hit per level with a 5-session gap
base_rate.rescanned: 2026-11-10 with fills at the reclaim; the earlier figures used the open

examples.limits: No RS rating or group (the 50-day and 200-day tests stood in), no market reading, daily bars only (the order of moves inside a day is unknown, and the owner enters intraday), survivors only, no costs. The same-day fill at L plus a cent assumes you were watching and bought the first trade back through the level. Nothing here is a published statistic.

8 closes under L 211.18 before the first close back above; the rule is 3 at most. A Remount (32-remount), bought on the retake of the line.
the 10-session low is only yesterday's low (104.91); a one-day dip under it and a close back over it is an Oops (30-oops-reversal), judged on one candle, not a U&R.
a same-day undercut (0.25%) and reclaim of L 409.58 with the close 9.7% under a falling 200-day SMA; the rule is a close above it. Watch only under B26.

question_seeds.seed: Within how many sessions must price close back above the level for a U&R, and how many closes under it turn the move into a Remount?
Where does the stop go on a U&R: under the level, or under the undercut low?
Does a U&R need a volume surge on the reclaim? What did Morales say, and what did the test find?
Hidden ticker: tap the level this stock undercut and reclaimed, and name what kind of level it is.
Hidden ticker: four reclaim days; tap the one that closed in the bottom half of its range and say why it grades lower.

conflicts: One setup or three: Undercut & Rally (multi-day, a prior low), the app's one-day Undercut & Reclaim (any level), and the MAU&R. The dossier leans to one lesson with the MAU&R as a named variant; the register folds the Wyckoff spring in too (D-002).

Which level: Morales's prior low in the pattern against the owner's any obvious level (prior highs, round numbers, gap lows, VWAP). The card lists the owner's levels; the register's default is (b) plus gap lows; the prior day's low alone is out either way (D-103).

Depth and time: Morales refuses a number; the dossier proposes 3% for an A, 6% at most, 3 sessions; the register's default is about 1 ATR and the same day for an A, 6% and 3 sessions as a B (D-036). The glossary closes the 4-close gap with the Remount: the U&R family runs to 4 closes, the Remount starts at 5.

The 200-day: Morales's best U&Rs come at market turns, often under or near the 200-day; B26 is hard. FIGR has no 200-day at all; the glossary's stand-in is the 50-day until 200 sessions exist (D-009).

Leader or mean reversion: the owner's leader U&R (RS 80 or more) against Bracco's washout mean reversion play, which C31 exempts; the register's default splits them by name (D-011). Whether the washout kind gets a 1 to 3 day plan is D-013.

The entry: the owner's intraday reclaim with confirmation against a close entry. The test shows why: at the close the pattern is not an edge (+0.06R against a +0.03R baseline); near the level every R number rises, but that row is biased upward because daily bars cannot see failed intraday reclaims (D-003).
C29 on post-earnings U&Rs: the owner's MXL was 40.9% over its 10-day (D-017).
Volume: the journal template's rising volume against Morales's generally not a factor; the test agrees with Morales (D-006).

The public scanner u_and_r.py credits Brian Shannon (the name is Morales and Kacher's), tells members U&Rs deliver 2:1+ RR in 70%+ of cases with no source, quotes Shannon and DeMark without a source, buys over the consolidation high (not the reclaim), stops 1.5% under the low, has no liquidity floor or 200-day rule, and gives sizing advice; the internal scanner uses $2 and $10,000, no 200-day rule, the stop exactly at the low, and fires on a third of eligible sessions. None of that reaches a member through this card (D-004, D-010).

The Study plan's counter-trend size smallest and tightest stop in the book are not the owner's practice (he trades U&Rs in leaders above their averages, once planned 30%+ of his account on one); size comes from E49 by grade.
Liquidity window: the dossier measures the $20 million on a 20-day average; the glossary's shared window is 50 sessions. The card says so on ur.liquidity.

The scan against the dossier's check: 50.2% to 3R with the fill at L plus a cent (same day, assumes you were watching) against 26% with a close entry (rescanned 2026-11-10 with fills at the reclaim; the earlier figures used the open); the earlier figure was 35.6%. The earlier scan also found the 1 to 3 session reclaim better than the same-day one; with fills at the reclaim the same-day reclaim is better (53.8% against 43.2%), mostly because its stop is tight (median 0.58%), while the check found them equal; the card quotes both.
